## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Closure chance against gauge level, one lock
      Objective: Estimate how one lock's closure chance moves with its upstream gauge level, from that lock's real closure history and real gauge readings.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (the package is empty)
      Produces: specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md (the curve, which lock and which data it used, and the measured cost); the fitted model in src/lock_closures, for later stages to reuse
      Exit: a closure-chance-versus-gauge-level curve for one lock, fitted on its real closure records and upstream gauge readings, recorded in the findings file; the findings file records the real run's measured cost: data volume pulled, load time and fit time
      Leaves out: traceability: suggested, see the approval question; the 7-day outlook: Ranked list item O2; the other 13 locks and pooling: Ranked list item O3; the operators' map: Ranked list item O4

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies
verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick
> the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every committed stage is ticked and the Ranked list is empty or parked,
re-run the gap rubric over the Outcomes list (O1–O4, plus any approved
outcomes), with evidence per verdict: implementing stage and plan, Deviation
notes, and deferred_items entries. Each unmet outcome becomes a new stage or a
conscious deferral with a written reason. Ranked-list items never promoted
park to `specs/deferred_items.md`.

---

Roadmap written to `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md`. It commits one stage, the core stage for Track A:

- **Stage 1 — Closure chance against gauge level, one lock (O1).** This stage fits the curve on one lock's real closure history and upstream gauge readings. It records the result and the measured cost of the run in `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`. It routes to brainstorming because the method is still open.
- **O2, O3 and O4** wait in the Ranked list in your order. Stage 1's measured fit time and data volume will firm up their cost notes before the next one is promoted.

One note on the tracks. O4 serves the boat operators, not the study, and it does not need O1's model. I should have pointed out that it could be its own track. As you ranked it, it waits behind O3. If you'd rather it go ahead on its own, say so in your answer.

**One question.** Do you approve this partition? It also includes one suggested quality:

- **Traceability.** The board funding the study will ask which gauge readings each closure estimate came from.
- **The outcome line it would become:** *"For each closure estimate, the gauge readings it came from (gauge, time, value), ready to show the trust's board."*

If you approve it, where should it go in the Ranked list relative to O2, O3 and O4? Or do you decline it?
